title: Staged recommendation cards with snapshot + reversible apply for Optimize console
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Build a staged recommendation card experience in the Optimize section of the Console that lets users preview diffs, capture runtime snapshots, apply configuration changes safely (canary/staged rollout), and perform quick rollback with a complete audit trail. The goal is to reduce manual tuning risk for batching/caching recommendations while preserving explainability and operator control.

Background and motivation: Teams frequently ignore automated batching and caching suggestions because they are unsure of runtime impact, fear regressions, or lack a clear rollback path. Current Optimize UI surfaces recommendations but lacks a safe apply flow, immutable snapshots, and a transparent audit trail tying changes to cost/latency metrics. This ticket defines the UX and acceptance criteria for cards, diff previews, and an apply-history model that engineering can implement in the console.

High-level requirements: 1) Recommendation cards show a succinct premise (expected unit cost delta, latency impact, confidence, primary rationale), example span of requests affected, and quick actions: Preview diff, Stage, Apply, Schedule. 2) Diff preview modal displays before/after config in a side-by-side, with simulated cost and latency delta using recent traffic. 3) Snapshot capture: before applying, capture a read-only snapshot of current serving config + runtime KPIs; snapshots are immutable and referenceable in history. 4) Safe apply: support canary (1%/10%/100%) rollout, automated health checks (error rate, latency SLOs, token error spikes) for automatic rollback, and manual rollback. 5) Audit trail: every stage/apply records actor, timestamp, snapshot id, diff id, and runtime check results; UI exposes a timeline with links to snapshots and the diff that was applied. 6) Undo semantics: a single-click revert that re-applies the snapshot config and records a reversal event. 7) Integrations: link to GitHub PR if config was generated from repo ops, and to a Confluence runbook for high-impact changes.

Edge cases and constraints: - Recommendations that require model changes or quantization profiles should be flagged as "requires engineer review" and not allow one-click apply. - For Dedicated/Private deployments, ensure the apply flow surfaces required approvals (RBAC) and KMS key rotation notes. - Large-scale changes affecting many routes should require scheduled maintenance window or an explicit override.

Metrics and success criteria: - Increase adoption of Optimize recommendations by 30% in 90 days post-launch. - Reduce manual rollback incidents by 50% (measured by reversal events) in 90 days. - Mean time to rollback < 5 minutes for staged failures. - At least one customer pilot completed with Dedicated tier teams within first 6 weeks.

Related artifacts and links: - Design exploration: https://drive.redwood.ai/optimize/cards-staged-v2 (mock link) - Diff preview spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPT/Diff+Preview+Spec - Security review notes: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/Sec/Optimize+apply+flow - Engineering spike PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1979
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation card presents concise delta (cost and latency) and confidence band
Diff preview shows side-by-side config + simulated KPI delta using 7d traffic sample
Apply flow requires snapshot creation and records snapshot id in audit trail
Support staged canary rollout with configurable buckets and automated health checks
Automatic rollback triggers on configurable thresholds and produces a reversal event in history
History/timeline UI lists stage/apply/revert events with links to snapshot diffs and actor metadata
RBAC/approval gate displayed for Dedicated/Private customers before apply
Changes that are non-runtime (model/quantization) are blocked from one-click apply and routed to engineer flow
